name: Haraza
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: language known only from a few dozen words (Bell 1975); no phonological description exists

sources.citation: Van Gerven Oei, Vincent W.J. & Angelika Jakobi (eds.). 2021. Dotawo: A Journal of Nubian Studies 7: Comparative Northern East Sudanic Linguistics. punctum books (CC BY-NC-ND). Contributions by G. Starostin ('Restoring "Nile-Nubian"…') and R. Blench ('Morphological Evidence for the Coherence of East Sudanic').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Starostin: 'Due to their poor documentation, the nearly extinct Birgid language of Darfur and the extinct Nubian language of Jebel Haraza are not considered in the present contribution' and 'the extinct and very poorly attested Haraza Nubian: auri-yah "two"' (citing Bell 1975: 10). Blench's table (c. p. 269) lists Haraza auri-yah from Bell. No accent marks, no prosodic remark.

sources.note: Silent on stress; ch. VII p. 103 notes only that peak-names at El Haraza, Um Durrag and Abu Hadid 'closely resemble Mídobi words' (Karshul, Kuriddi, Kurkayla, Kaludi, Karshennad); no wordlist of the language.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page hara1258 and reference records 38818, 98177, 149937, 122717.
sources.note: All three Haraza-specific references are typed 'Wordlist or less' (Bell 1975: 18 words counted; Mohamed 1974: 14; Newbold 1924: 6). No grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Haraza language' (raw wikitext) and Nubian Languages and Culture Project, 'Haraza - an extinct Nubian language' (nubianlanguagesandculture.org).
sources.note: Wikipedia: 'known only from a few dozen words recalled by village elders in 1923' (citing Bell 1975; Rilly 2010: 166). The NLCP page has a photograph of the last speaker (Shaikh 'Umar Ya'sin Dawalib Abd al Hadi, photo by Herman Bell, 1960s) and no linguistic content.

sources.citation: Rilly, Claude. 2010. Le méroïtique et sa famille linguistique. Afrique et Langage 14. Leuven/Paris: Peeters, p. 166 and Haraza entries in the comparative lexicon.
